question.text: Mr. Verma, a Central Government employee under the new tax regime, contributes Rs. 1,50,000 to NPS Tier I under Section 80CCD(1) and an additional Rs. 50,000 under Section 80CCD(1B). His basic + DA is Rs. 70,000 per month (annual Rs. 8,40,000), and his employer contributes 14% of basic + DA to NPS. Applying the 10% of salary cap on employee 80CCD(1), the overall Section 80C/80CCC/80CCD(1) ceiling of Rs. 1,50,000, the Rs. 50,000 limit under 80CCD(1B), and the 14% government-employer cap under 80CCD(2), what is his total NPS-related tax deduction?

answer.text: Rs. 3,17,600, but the employee's 80CCD(1) deduction is subject to the overall 80C ceiling of Rs. 1,50,000, so net additional benefit is 80CCD(1B) Rs. 50,000 + employer's 80CCD(2) Rs. 1,17,600
Rs. 2,67,600 (Rs. 1,50,000 under 80CCD(1) capped at Rs. 1,00,000 + Rs. 50,000 under 80CCD(1B) + employer's 14%)

explanation.text: The Logic: NPS tax deductions operate across three sections. (1) 80CCD(1): employee contribution is capped at 10% of salary (basic + DA) and falls within the overall Rs. 1,50,000 ceiling of Section 80C/80CCC/80CCD(1). For Mr. Verma, 10% of Rs. 8,40,000 = Rs. 84,000 is the 80CCD(1) cap from the salary test, but the overall 80C umbrella caps it at Rs. 1,50,000 only if other 80C investments do not already consume the limit. (2) 80CCD(1B): an additional Rs. 50,000 over and above the 80C limit. (3) 80CCD(2): employer contribution up to 14% of basic + DA for Central Government employees (10% for other employers), and this is over and above the 80C/80CCD(1B) ceiling. Employer contribution = 14% x Rs. 70,000 x 12 = Rs. 1,17,600. Maximum total = Rs. 1,50,000 (within 80C) + Rs. 50,000 (80CCD(1B)) + Rs. 1,17,600 (80CCD(2)) = Rs. 3,17,600. The Trap: The first option ignores the employer contribution entirely. The key nuance is that 80CCD(1) is not in addition to 80C, it sits within the 80C umbrella, so only 80CCD(1B) and 80CCD(2) are truly additional. Candidates also miss that the 14% employer cap applies only to Central Government employees and that the 10% of salary cap on 80CCD(1) must be checked before applying the Rs. 1,50,000 umbrella. Note: The answer assumes Central Government employer status and that the tax regime in force permits these deductions; under the new regime, 80CCD(2) employer contribution remains deductible while 80CCD(1) and 80CCD(1B) generally do not. The figures here illustrate the maximum deduction position under the assumptions stated in the stem.
